title: Founders Week kickoff remarks + rapid FAQ (scratchpad)
content:
Context / goal (notes to self):
- Short, human opening to start Founders Week — set tone: gratitude, clarity about what to expect this week (celebration + signals for the year).
- Keep remarks 6-7 minutes max. One personal anecdote, one product/ops update, two forward-looking signals.
- Follow with a 10–12 minute fireside + open mic. Have a 3-question rapid FAQ ready if audience quiet.

Outline (high level):
1) Greeting & thanks (30s)
   - Quick hello, acknowledge remote folks and new hires.
   - Call out that this week is about community and focus: celebrate wins, learn together, align on next priorities.

2) One short story (60–90s)
   - Personal: earliest memory working on inference - first time a model shipped and a customer called to tell us "it changed a workflow for them". Keep it human (mention kitchen-table hack sessions, late-night deploy).

3) Where we are (90s)
   - Quick signal: product maturity + scale. Mention hosted API momentum + Dedicated traction + Private deals progressing.
   - Important metric: emphasize reliability focus rather than raw growth numbers here (e.g., reduced P99 latency by X% year-over-year — placeholder).

4) What matters next (90s)
   - Two clear priorities: (1) Deliver predictable latency and unit economics; (2) Expand private deployments + compliance.
   - Connect to developer experience: docs, SDKs, and rollout tooling are not "nice-to-haves" — they are core.

5) Culture note (30s)
   - Small teams, big impact. Encourage cross-team pairing during Founders Week sessions.

6) Call to action (30s)
   - Join 3 events this week: Tech deep-dive on serving runtime, Customer case study session, and the cross-functional hack-hour.

Rapid FAQ (for fireside / post-remarks) — keep answers 1–2 sentences: 
Q1: Are we hiring aggressively this year?
A: Yes — focus on infra/serving runtime, SRE, and customer-facing engineering for Dedicated/Private. Hiring plan ties to usage-driven thresholds; recruiting updates will come after this quarter's review.

Q2: Will pricing change with Dedicated contracts?
A: No surprise increases planned. We're experimenting with clearer bundling and usage tiers to make cost predictable — we'll share specifics in the Dedicated product meeting.

Q3: How are we handling model regressions / quality drift?
A: Multi-pronged: automated quality checks on rollout, prompt/eval suites, and an ops playbook that can rollback model variants quickly. Alerts are routed to product + SRE on regressions.

Anticipated tougher questions & suggested responses (notes to self):
- "Why didn't we hit our latency SLO last month?" — Be transparent: specific root cause (e.g., mem-leak in KV cache layer + unexpected traffic pattern). Explain fix timeline and monitoring changes.
- "Are we partnering with hardware vendors?" — Yes, highlight selective partnerships for benchmarking and early access to new GPU families; emphasize portability of our runtime.
- "Can we open-source parts of the runtime?" — We will continue to share tooling, but core runtime IP is strategic; consider targeted OSS experiments (benchmarks, connectivity libs).

Tone cues (internal):
- Keep it candid, not corporate-polished. Use plain‑English sentences. Avoid heavy product marketing jargon.
- Encourage curiosity: phrases like "we still have a lot to learn here" and "help us test this" invite participation.

Logistics / checklist (to-do for event):
- Confirm AV and captioning (Sofia) by Tue EOD.
- Final slide deck to comms by Wed morning (Ethan).
- Print 4-line cheat-sheet for founders (name + 3 bullets) for stage use.
- Slack post draft for announcement and event RSVP link.

Reminders for the actual delivery (Riya notes):
- Pause after the anecdote — let the room react.
- Lead with gratitude — people appreciate specific shout-outs.
- If a technical deep-dive audience asks too many specifics, offer a follow-up session with eng leads.

Loose draft script (speakable):
Hi everyone — welcome to Founders Week. It feels a little like a family reunion — we get to stop the day-to-day and celebrate the little wins, and also ask the blunt questions we sometimes push aside. I remember the first time I watched a customer replace a manual workflow with something our API enabled — someone on the other end of the line said, 'This saved my team a day each week.' That stuck with me because it made the work real.

Right now, we're standing on three things: a serving runtime that can actually be trusted in production, a set of customers telling us the product matters, and a team that knows how to move fast. This year our north stars are simple: make inference predictable (latency and cost), and make deploying privately as frictionless as hosted. If we do those well, we unlock a lot more product-led growth and enterprise confidence.

There will be a bunch of sessions this week — please join the ones that matter to you. Meet folks you haven't worked with. Tell us honestly what's broken. And if you only come to one talk, come to the runtime deep-dive — the engineers are doing a live demo of batching and cache heuristics.

Thanks for everything you do — now let's get into it.

Post-event follow-ups (scratch):
- Send summary + recording link within 24 hours.
- Collect 3 quick feedback Qs in the RSVP form (use anonymous option).
- Track follow-up items in a Founders Week board (link in slack).

Random notes / fragments (keep for later):
- Consider a "Hall of Wins" email chain where teams post a single screenshot + 1-liner each day.
- Possible founder office hours timeslots: Thu 11–12 & Fri 3–4.
- If fireside goes long: have a soft wrap script ready to push to breakout rooms.

End of scratchpad.

(Internal — do not share externally)
